The likelihood of our system moving in the same plane as the entire galaxy, or orthogonally to the galaxy is very slim given the VAST number of other angles it can move.

I think with gravity in play the vast amounts of angles becomes very slim. Saturn's rings are generally only 30 feet deep at its thickest point, thats extremely thin on the planetary scale. Well, rings and orbits level out because of the cancellation of forces. MinutePhysics did a pretty good video on it, and why most orbits are in the same plane. But this doesn't come into play when an entire system is moving freely through space. Without this three-dimensional interaction and cancellation of forces, movement can happen in literally any direction. This means that the system can move in any direction in three dimensions. So for our system to move in one of two directions (in planar space with the galaxy, or in orthogonal space with the galaxy like this gif) is extremely unlikely. It's far more likely for us to be on some sort of tilt as there's an infinite number of angles that aren't one of those two.
